docs.text:
Platform Repository configuration Updates after connection GitHub Pages .github/workflows/docs.yml Enabled; updates automatically after a push to main Read the Docs .readthedocs.yaml A webhook triggers builds after importing the repository Cloudflare Pages wrangler.toml and the settings below Builds automatically after connecting the GitHub repository GitLab Pages .gitlab-ci.yml and optional GitHub sync job GitHub pushes source to GitLab, then GitLab CI publishes it GitBook Generated gitbook-zh and gitbook-en branches Two Spaces sync their branches and publish as language variants

GitHub Pages is live. Configuration and content exports are ready for the other four platforms; their first publication requires creating or linking a project in the corresponding account.

docs.title: GitHub Pages
docs.text:
After pushing documentation to main, open the repository's Documentation workflow. It builds the site, updates gh-pages, and requests a Pages build.

Chinese uses the site root; English uses en/. The language menu opens the other-language version of the current page.

docs.title: Read the Docs
docs.text:
1. Sign into Read the Docs and import lz59970062/long-task-wakeup.
  2. Select main, use the root .readthedocs.yaml, and choose Simplified Chinese as the project language.
  3. Trigger the first build, open the assigned public URL, and check the language menu.
  4. Confirm the GitHub webhook is connected in the project's integration settings so future pushes rebuild it.

Each build contains both languages. The build hook reads READTHEDOCS_CANONICAL_URL so language links and the sitemap use the hosted site's full path. See the Read the Docs MkDocs guide.

docs.title: Cloudflare Pages
docs.text:
Create a Pages project under Workers & Pages, connect the same GitHub repository, and enter:

Setting Value Production branch main Root directory Repository root Build command pip install -r docs/requirements.txt && python scripts/docs_sync.py check && mkdocs build --strict Build output directory site Environment variable PYTHON_VERSION=3.12

wrangler.toml also sets site as the output directory. The site URL comes from CF_PAGES_URL. For a custom domain, set LTC_DOCS_SITE_URL to the full public URL. See Cloudflare's MkDocs deployment guide.

docs.title: GitLab Pages
docs.text:
Create an empty GitLab project with main as the default branch. In the GitHub repository, open Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions and add:

Type Name Value Repository variable DOCS_GITLAB_REPOSITORY The GitLab project's HTTPS clone URL Repository secret DOCS_GITLAB_TOKEN An access token with write_repository permission for that project

Keep the token in GitHub Secrets. Run the Documentation workflow manually once. Its sync-gitlab job pushes the current commit to GitLab's main; subsequent documentation updates repeat the sync. GitLab builds and publishes site using .gitlab-ci.yml, with CI_PAGES_URL as the site address.

Find the public URL under Deploy → Pages in GitLab and enable public Pages access. The configuration uses pages.publish from GitLab 17.10 or later. See the GitLab Pages guide.

docs.title: GitBook
docs.text:
GitHub Actions generates two content branches. Each contains Markdown, SUMMARY.md, .gitbook.yaml, and a sync-manifest.json recording the source commit.

  1. Create a Chinese Space and an English Space in GitBook.
  2. Enable Git Sync for each Space. Connect Chinese to this repository's gitbook-zh branch and English to gitbook-en.
  3. Choose to import content from GitHub for the first sync. SUMMARY.md supplies the table of contents.
  4. Add both Spaces to the same documentation site as language variants, named “​简体中文​” and “English,” then publish.

Continue editing source files in docs/ on main. The workflow updates both export branches, which GitBook syncs. During export, MkDocs buttons become ordinary links and installation tabs become section headings. Follow the GitBook language variants tutorial for site configuration.

Inspect the exports locally with:

python scripts/docs_sync.py export

The files are written to build/gitbook/zh/ and build/gitbook/en/.

docs.title: Check a sync
docs.text:
Confirm that GitHub's Documentation build passed, then open a newly updated page on the destination platform. Switch languages and check code blocks, internal links, and search. Compare the source commit in GitBook's sync-manifest.json with the GitHub commit you published.

Use LTC_DOCS_SITE_URL to override automatic URL detection for a custom domain. Set it to the complete site-root URL, including the trailing /.
